description: Verify that users can filter products within a specified price range and view appropriate results.
steps: Locate the 'Min price' and 'Max price' fields.
Input a value of 50 in the 'Min price' field.
Input a value of 150 in the 'Max price' field.
Click the 'FILTER' button to apply the price range filter.
Wait for the filtered products list to load.
Verify that all displayed products have prices within the range of 50 to 150.
expected_results: Products displayed are within the specified price range of 50 to 150.
No products with prices outside the range appear in the filtered list.
edge_cases: User inputs non-numeric values in the 'Min price' or 'Max price' fields.
User sets 'Min price' greater than 'Max price'.
No products are available within the specified range.
User attempts to filter without setting values in both fields.
User sets an extremely large or small price range.
data_requirements: Products with varying prices available in the store.
Minimum and maximum price thresholds defined in the backend.
Valid HTML structure for filter elements.
Accurate price data for each product.
Responsive design to adapt to user actions.
dependencies: Product price data must be accurate and up-to-date.
The filter functionality must be implemented in the backend.
The store page must be accessible.
api_interactions: API call to fetch products based on the applied filter.
Error handling for invalid inputs in price fields.
performance_metrics: Filter response time should be under 2 seconds.
Ensure no UI lag while applying filters.
accessibility_requirements: Labels must be readable and accessible via screen readers.
Ensure the filter buttons are keyboard navigable.
Field errors must be announced clearly for invalid input.
